s0301.literal: On yimao day, because Ansa, civil administration officer concurrently commanding the Huaimeng and other armies, died in battle at Bianliang, his son Mangudai was appointed wanhu and granted a gold tally.
s0301.idiomatic: On yimao day Ansa, who had commanded the Huaimeng armies while serving as a civil administration officer, fell at Bianliang; his son Mangudai was made wanhu and given a gold tally.

s0302.literal: On wuwu day, six hundred field households were granted to Xianzhen.
s0302.idiomatic: On wuwu day Xianzhen received six hundred field households.

s0303.literal: On jiwei day, five hundred sheep were granted to King Wang Chon of Goryeo.
s0303.idiomatic: On jiwei day King Wang Chon of Goryeo was granted five hundred sheep.

s0304.literal: On guiyou day, one thousand ingots of notes were granted to Princess Baihu's domain.
s0304.idiomatic: On guiyou day one thousand ingots of notes were granted to the households under Princess Baihu.

s0305.literal: A Public Benevolence Medicine Bureau was established at Shangdu.
s0305.idiomatic: A public-benefit pharmacy bureau was opened at Shangdu.

s0306.literal: A temple to Emperor Yao was built at Pingyang, and fifteen qing of fields were granted besides.
s0306.idiomatic: A temple to Emperor Yao was built at Pingyang, with fifteen qing of fields granted to support it.

s0307.literal: Xianzhen was made Right Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat and Tachar Left Grand Councillor.
s0307.idiomatic: Xianzhen was appointed Right Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat and Tachar Left Grand Councillor.

s0308.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on guiwei day, an edict ordered appanage princes not to summon on their own authority officials of the Yanjing circuit prefectures and counties.
s0308.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on guiwei day, an edict forbade appanage princes to detain Yanjing circuit prefectural and county officials on their own authority.

s0309.literal: On yiyou day, people at the field camp at Wild Fox Ridge were forbidden to enter the Southern or Northern passes to graze livestock and damage mulberry crops and grain.
s0309.idiomatic: On yiyou day people at the Wild Fox Ridge field camp were forbidden to drive livestock through the Southern or Northern passes and trample mulberry fields and grain.

s0310.literal: Princess Baihu was given fifty thousand taels of silver, and Qaraqana one thousand taels of silver.
s0310.idiomatic: Princess Baihu received fifty thousand taels of silver, and Qaraqana one thousand taels.

s0311.literal: On yiwei day, because the late acting wanhu of Dongping, Lü Yi, died in the service of the state, he was posthumously given the honorific title Zhenjie.
s0311.idiomatic: On yiwei day Lü Yi, the late acting wanhu of Dongping who had died in state service, was posthumously honored with the title Zhenjie.

s0312.literal: On wuxu day, an edict relaxed the prohibition on weapons along Henan's border.
s0312.idiomatic: On wuxu day an edict eased the ban on weapons along the Henan frontier.

s0313.literal: Anci County in Yanjing Circuit was promoted to Dong'an Prefecture, and Gu'an to Gu'an Prefecture.
s0313.idiomatic: Anci County in Yanjing circuit was elevated to Dong'an Prefecture, and Gu'an to Gu'an Prefecture.

s0314.literal: The Henan Army Control Commission reported: "The garrison-farming populace serving as local-defense archer troops and scout soldiers totaled three thousand four hundred; they were divided to garrison border prefectures and counties, and they request exemption from other corvée obligations.
s0314.idiomatic: The Henan army control commission reported that three thousand four hundred garrison-farming men serving as local-defense archers and scouts had been posted to border prefectures and counties, and asked that their other corvée duties be remitted.

s0316.literal: On gengzi day, an edict granted Prince Jadu sixty-three thousand one hundred taels of silver as payment for oxen and horses.
s0316.idiomatic: On gengzi day an edict granted Prince Jadu sixty-three thousand one hundred taels of silver to cover ox and horse costs.

s0317.literal: On renyin day, an edict forbade tamaci in the Yidu Route from molesting the people.
s0317.idiomatic: On renyin day an edict forbade tamaci in Yidu circuit from harassing civilians.

s0318.literal: The Chengdu Pacification Commission was placed under the Western Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
s0318.idiomatic: The Chengdu pacification commission was subordinated to the Western Sichuan branch secretariat.

s0319.literal: Mongols, Han troops, and others were forbidden to boil and sell private salt.
s0319.idiomatic: Mongols, Han soldiers, and others were forbidden to produce or traffic in illicit salt.

s0320.literal: An edict ordered the Shandong Pacification Commission to move the people of Jiao, Lai, Ju, and Mi and the salt households inland.
s0320.idiomatic: An edict told the Shandong pacification commission to relocate the people of Jiao, Lai, Ju, and Mi and the salt households inland.

s0321.literal: Central Secretariat ministers said this would obstruct salt boiling; thereupon the Army Control Commission was ordered to restore the border garrisons, and resident and salt households were not to be moved.
s0321.idiomatic: Secretariat ministers warned that the move would disrupt salt production, so the army control commission was ordered to restore the border garrisons and leave resident and salt households in place.

s0322.literal: An edict ordered Aju to warn the Mongol army not to use civilian fields as pasture.
s0322.idiomatic: An edict told Aju to warn Mongol troops not to turn civilian farmland into pasture.

s0323.literal: Attached counties in the Yanjing, Hejian, Kaiping, and Longxing circuits were harmed by hail that damaged the crops.
s0323.idiomatic: Attached counties in Yanjing, Hejian, Kaiping, and Longxing were hit by hail that destroyed the crops.

s0324.literal: Eighth month, on wushen new moon, an edict ordered Huomuhai to supervise relay stations in all circuits and granted him a gold tally.
s0324.idiomatic: On the wushen new moon of the eighth month an edict put Huomuhai in charge of relay stations in every circuit and granted him a gold tally.

s0325.literal: On xinhai day, a Marshal's Headquarters was established at Dali.
s0325.idiomatic: On xinhai day a marshal's headquarters was established at Dali.

s0326.literal: An edict ordered the Dongping, Daming, and Henan Pacification Commissions to purchase one thousand five hundred fifty horses for the armies of Aju and others.
s0326.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Dongping, Daming, and Henan pacification commissions to buy one thousand five hundred fifty horses for Aju's army and others.

s0327.literal: Xuan Prefecture was promoted to Xuande Prefecture and placed under Shangdu.
s0327.idiomatic: Xuan Prefecture was elevated to Xuande Prefecture and placed under Shangdu.

s0328.literal: Zi, Lai, and Deng prefectures were combined into a Route General Command, with its seat at Zi Prefecture.
s0328.idiomatic: Zi, Lai, and Deng were combined into a route general command headquartered at Zi Prefecture.

s0329.literal: Sisaxi was ordered to take overall control of the Ghost Country and Dali routes.
s0329.idiomatic: Sisaxi was ordered to take overall control of the Ghost Country and Dali routes.

s0330.literal: Liu Fang, Director in the Ministry of Rites, who had earlier been envoy to Dali, was killed by bandits when he reached Tibet; an edict ordered his family comforted.
s0330.idiomatic: Liu Fang of the Ministry of Rites, who had earlier served as envoy to Dali, was killed by bandits in Tibet; the court ordered his family compensated.

s0331.literal: On renzi day, the Central Secretariat was ordered to supply paper money for cart and ox costs to the Beijing and Western Capital transport commissions.
s0331.idiomatic: On renzi day the Central Secretariat was told to provide notes for cart and ox costs to the Beijing and Western Capital transport commissions.

s0332.literal: Zhangde Circuit and Ming and Ci prefectures suffered drought; half of this year's field rent in Zhangde was remitted, and six-tenths in Ming and Ci.
s0332.idiomatic: Zhangde circuit and Ming and Ci prefectures suffered drought; half of Zhangde's field rent for the year was remitted, and six-tenths in Ming and Ci.

s0333.literal: Axi and others, Mongol centurions of Ji Prefecture, violated the salt prohibition; more than one hundred twenty horses were confiscated and given to soldiers without mounts.
s0333.idiomatic: Axi and other Mongol centurions of Ji Prefecture broke the salt ban; more than one hundred twenty of their horses were seized and given to soldiers who lacked mounts.

s0334.literal: On jiayin day, Chengdu Circuit was ordered to transport ten thousand shi of grain to provision Tongchuan.
s0334.idiomatic: On jiayin day Chengdu circuit was ordered to ship ten thousand shi of grain to Tongchuan.

s0335.literal: Paper money was issued to Liu Zheng to purchase oxen for garrison farming.
s0335.idiomatic: Notes were issued to Liu Zheng to buy oxen for garrison farming.

s0336.literal: Liu Yuanli's army and others were divided to garrison Tongchuan, and Andun was ordered to command them.
s0336.idiomatic: Forces under Liu Yuanli and others were posted to garrison Tongchuan under Andun's command.

s0337.literal: On bingchen day, an edict ordered Mian Prefecture in Chengdu Circuit placed under Tongchuan.
s0337.idiomatic: On bingchen day an edict placed Mian Prefecture in Chengdu circuit under Tongchuan.

s0338.literal: On wuwu day, Atu and Shang Ting were placed in charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs at Chengdu; the grand marshal headquarters of Chengdu, Shunqing, and Tongchuan were all placed under their control.
s0338.idiomatic: On wuwu day Atu and Shang Ting were put in charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs at Chengdu, with the Chengdu, Shunqing, and Tongchuan grand marshal headquarters all under their command.

s0339.literal: On gengshen day, because Shi Tianni had earlier been killed by Wu Xian, Wu Xian's residence was granted to his son Ji.
s0339.idiomatic: On gengshen day, because Shi Tianni had earlier been killed by Wu Xian, Wu Xian's residence was granted to Tianni's son Ji.

s0340.literal: On guihai day, an edict ordered Jingzhao Circuit to grant Liu Zheng one residence and twenty qing of fields.
s0340.idiomatic: On guihai day an edict ordered Jingzhao circuit to grant Liu Zheng one residence and twenty qing of fields.

s0341.literal: Because the people under Manggubala were impoverished, seven thousand five hundred taels of silver were granted to relieve them.
s0341.idiomatic: Because Manggubala's followers were impoverished, seven thousand five hundred taels of silver were granted for their relief.

s0342.literal: On jiazi day, because the Western Liang region had suffered warfare and the people were exhausted, paper money was issued for relief, and rents and levies were remitted for three years.
s0342.idiomatic: On jiazi day, because warfare had worn down Western Liang and its people, notes were issued for relief and rents and levies were waived for three years.

s0343.literal: An edict ordered that when ministers transmitted imperial instructions, any point of doubt had to be reported back for confirmation.
s0343.idiomatic: An edict required ministers transmitting imperial instructions to report back for confirmation whenever a point was doubtful.

s0344.literal: On bingyin day, because the people under Prince Jibtemür were destitute, twenty thousand taels of silver were granted to relieve them.
s0344.idiomatic: On bingyin day, because Prince Jibtemür's followers were destitute, twenty thousand taels of silver were granted for their relief.

s0345.literal: On renshen day, express relay stations were re-established.
s0345.idiomatic: On renshen day express relay stations were restored.

s0346.literal: Bin and Di prefectures suffered locusts; Zhending Circuit suffered drought.
s0346.idiomatic: Locusts struck Bin and Di prefectures, and Zhending circuit suffered drought.

s0347.literal: An edict ordered that Western Liang refugees who returned to their occupations should have their households exempted for three years.
s0347.idiomatic: An edict ordered that Western Liang refugees who returned to their occupations should have their households exempted from levies for three years.

s0348.literal: The imperial carriage arrived from Shangdu.

s0349.literal: Ninth month, on renwu day, eighteen Song spies — Wang Li, Zhang Da, Diao Jun, and others — captured by the Henan and Daming Pacification Commissions were released under the general amnesty, given clothing, and sent home.
s0349.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renwu day, eighteen Song spies captured by the Henan and Daming pacification commissions — Wang Li, Zhang Da, Diao Jun, and others — were freed under the general amnesty, clothed, and sent home.

s0350.literal: On yiyou day, the Grain Transport River and Canal Office was established.
s0350.idiomatic: On yiyou day the grain transport river-and-canal office was established.

s0351.literal: On jichou day, seed grain and ox implements were granted to the people under Prince Ajigi.
s0351.idiomatic: On jichou day seed grain and ox implements were granted to Prince Ajigi's followers.

s0352.literal: On gengyin day, Goryeo, Shangjing, and other places were instructed not to impose heavy levies on the people.
s0352.idiomatic: On gengyin day Goryeo, Shangjing, and other districts were told not to impose heavy levies on the people.

s0353.literal: Refugees in Jinan and Bin-Di were summoned to return.
s0353.idiomatic: Refugees in Jinan and Bin-Di were called back to their homes.

s0354.literal: Envoys were dispatched to collect taxes in money and silk from all circuits.
s0354.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to collect tax payments in money and silk from every circuit.

s0355.literal: Cloth and silk sold among the people that was loose-woven, thin, or short in width was forbidden.
s0355.idiomatic: The sale of loose-woven, thin, or narrow cloth and silk in private markets was forbidden.

s0356.literal: Winter, tenth month, on wuwu day, relays in the Longxing Route were first established.
s0356.idiomatic: On wuwu day of the tenth month of winter relay stations in Longxing circuit were established for the first time.

s0357.literal: Eleventh month, on jiashen day, an edict ordered that because the harvest had failed, field rations for the Ashu and Qielie armies be reduced proportionally.
s0357.idiomatic: On jiashen day of the eleventh month an edict ordered field rations for the Ashu and Qielie armies cut proportionally because the harvest had failed.

s0358.literal: Dongping, Daming, and other circuits suffered drought; this year's field rent was reduced proportionally.
s0358.idiomatic: Dongping, Daming, and other circuits suffered drought, and field rents for the year were cut proportionally.

s0359.literal: On bingxu day, sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, with Qidan, Tachar, Wang Pan, and Zhang Wenqian performing the rites.
s0359.idiomatic: On bingxu day sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, with Qidan, Tachar, Wang Pan, and Zhang Wenqian conducting the rites.

s0360.literal: King Wang Chon of Goryeo, on account of the abolition of relay stations and household registration and other matters, sent his minister Han Jiu with a memorial of thanks; the Zhongtong fifth-year calendar and one bolt of Shu brocade were granted, and Chon was also ordered to come to court.
s0360.idiomatic: King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent his minister Han Jiu with a memorial of thanks over the abolition of relay stations, household registration, and related measures; he received the fifth-year Zhongtong calendar and a bolt of Shu brocade, and was ordered to come to court.

s0361.literal: The Imperial Garments Bureau and Imperial Provisions Bureau were established.
s0361.idiomatic: The Imperial Garments Bureau and Imperial Provisions Bureau were established.

s0362.literal: Twelfth month, on dingwei new moon, the Fengxiang garrison troops, Wang Weizheng's Qingju army, and Diao Guoqi's Pingyang army were placed under Yidu Grand Marshal Qincha to garrison Huxiao Stockade.
s0362.idiomatic: On the dingwei new moon of the twelfth month the Fengxiang garrison, Wang Weizheng's Qingju force, and Diao Guoqi's Pingyang force were placed under Yidu Grand Marshal Qincha to garrison Huxiao Stockade.

s0363.literal: On jiaxu day, an edict ordered the grape households of the imperial son-in-law Aibuhua to pay taxes according to the civilian rule.
s0363.idiomatic: On jiaxu day an edict ordered the grape households of the imperial son-in-law Aibuhua to pay taxes on the same terms as civilians.

s0364.literal: Nestorian Christians, Dasman, monks, and Daoists who farmed land were to pay rent; those who traded were to pay tax.
s0364.idiomatic: Nestorian Christians, Dasman, monks, and Daoists who farmed paid land rent, and those who traded paid commercial tax.

s0365.literal: On bingzi day, the princes were granted gold, silver, bolts, and silk according to the annual custom.
s0365.idiomatic: On bingzi day princes received gold, silver, bolts, and silk as in the annual custom.

s0366.literal: That year throughout the empire there were 1,579,110 households;
s0366.idiomatic: That year the empire registered 1,579,110 households;

s0367.literal: In levies: 706,401 jin of silk and 49,487 ingots of notes;
s0367.idiomatic: Levies came to 706,401 jin of silk and 49,487 ingots of notes;

s0368.literal: Seven persons were sentenced to death.
s0368.idiomatic: Seven persons were sentenced to death.

s0369.literal: Second month, on xinhai day, He Fu and five others reported unregistered households in Pingyang and Taiyuan; an edict offered official reward, but court ministers deemed them unqualified for office and paper money was given instead.
s0369.idiomatic: On xinhai day of the second month He Fu and five others reported unregistered households in Pingyang and Taiyuan; the court offered official reward, but ministers judged them unfit for office and paid them in notes instead.

s0370.literal: An edict ordered the selection of Confucian scholars to compile the national history, translate the classics, establish halls of residence, and grant salaries for their support.
s0370.idiomatic: An edict ordered Confucian scholars chosen to compile the national history, translate the classics, and be housed and salaried for the work.

s0371.literal: On renzi day, Qionghua Island was restored.
s0371.idiomatic: On renzi day Qionghua Island was restored.

s0372.literal: The army under Beijing Grand Marshal Ahai was ordered to dredge the Shuangta grain canal.
s0372.idiomatic: The army under Beijing Grand Marshal Ahai was ordered to dredge the Shuangta grain canal.

s0373.literal: On jiayin day, because the late qianhu of Bozhou, Di Run, had been lost to the Song, his son Rongzu was ordered to succeed to the post.
s0373.idiomatic: On jiayin day, because the late qianhu of Bozhou, Di Run, had fallen to the Song, his son Rongzu was ordered to inherit the post.

s0374.literal: On bingchen day, the Shaanxi Branch Ministry of Revenue was abolished.
s0374.idiomatic: On bingchen day the Shaanxi branch Ministry of Revenue was abolished.

s0375.literal: On dingmao day, the moon encroached on Nandou.
s0375.idiomatic: On dingmao day the moon passed through Nandou.

s0376.literal: On guiyou day, the imperial carriage went to Shangdu.
s0376.idiomatic: On guiyou day the Emperor went to Shangdu.

s0377.literal: An edict ordered route administrators Shi Quan and twenty-two others to come to Shangdu for the great court assembly.
s0377.idiomatic: An edict summoned route administrators Shi Quan and twenty-two others to Shangdu for the great court assembly.

s0378.literal: The prohibition on weapons in the border cities was relaxed.
s0378.idiomatic: The ban on weapons in the border cities was eased.

s0379.literal: Third month, on gengchen day, the Grand Heaven Ritual was established at Changchun Palace.
s0379.idiomatic: On gengchen day of the third month the Grand Heaven Ritual was instituted at Changchun Palace.

s0380.literal: On jihai day, Minister Song Zizhen was ordered to set forth current affairs; Zizhen submitted them item by item, an edict praised and encouraged him, and the Central Secretariat was ordered to deliberate and implement them.
s0380.idiomatic: On jihai day Minister Song Zizhen was ordered to report on current affairs; he submitted a detailed list, received an edict of praise, and the Central Secretariat was told to deliberate and carry out his proposals.

s0381.literal: On xinchou day, an edict to the Sichuan Branch Secretariat ordered Atu to take exclusive charge of military affairs, while Shang Ting would handle criminal cases, finances, and grain.
s0381.idiomatic: On xinchou day an edict to the Sichuan branch secretariat put Atu in sole charge of military affairs and left criminal cases, finances, and grain to Shang Ting.

s0382.literal: The Grain Transport Commission was established, with Wang Guangyi as commissioner.
s0382.idiomatic: The grain transport commission was established, with Wang Guangyi as commissioner.

s0383.literal: Summer, fourth month, on wushen day, because the Zhangde and Ming-Ci circuits had drawn the Zhang, Fu, and Huan rivers to irrigate fields, causing the Imperial Canal to shoal and salt transport to be blocked, branch channels were filled in to restore the water flow.
s0383.idiomatic: On wushen day of the fourth month of summer, because Zhangde and Ming-Ci had diverted the Zhang, Fu, and Huan rivers to irrigate fields and left the Imperial Canal too shallow for salt transport, branch channels were blocked off to restore the current.

s0384.literal: On xinhai day, the moon encroached on the Woman star in the Xuanyuan asterism.
s0384.idiomatic: On xinhai day the moon passed through the Woman star in Xuanyuan.

s0385.literal: On renzi day, Dongping, Taiyuan, and Pingyang suffered drought; Western monks were dispatched separately to pray for rain.
s0385.idiomatic: On renzi day Dongping, Taiyuan, and Pingyang suffered drought, and Western monks were sent out separately to pray for rain.

s0386.literal: On yimao day, an edict ordered King Wang Chon of Goryeo to come to Shangdu and perform the ceremony due from a vassal who attends in person.
s0386.idiomatic: On yimao day an edict ordered King Wang Chon of Goryeo to come to Shangdu and perform the ceremony owed by a vassal attending in person.

s0387.literal: On xinyou day, Sichuan tea, salt, commercial, wine, and bamboo levies were assigned to supply army grain.
s0387.idiomatic: On xinyou day Sichuan levies on tea, salt, commerce, wine, and bamboo were assigned to supply army grain.

s0388.literal: Yang Dayuan, because his subordinate Wang Zhong had obtained a letter from the Song general Zan Wanshou and killed him, received an edict stating that since the matter had not yet been investigated, he might have fallen into a Song stratagem — how could execution be applied so rashly? Dayuan was rebuked, and Wang Zhong's family was still to be comforted.
s0388.idiomatic: Yang Dayuan's subordinate Wang Zhong had killed a man after obtaining a letter from the Song general Zan Wanshou; an edict rebuked Dayuan, saying that without investigation he might have played into a Song ruse and should not have ordered execution so hastily, and Wang Zhong's family was to be compensated.

s0389.literal: Nanjiadai, an official of the imperial park, requested repair of the imperial resting cool pavilion and expansion of pasture land; an edict ordered the cool pavilion deferred until an agricultural lull, and pasture land divided among farmers without fields.
s0389.idiomatic: Nanjiadai, an imperial park official, asked to repair the imperial resting cool pavilion and expand pasture; the court deferred the pavilion until the farming slack season and ordered pasture land divided among landless farmers.

s0390.literal: On dingmao day, the crimes of Zhang Bangzhi the wanhu, his brothers, and twenty-seven others including Jiang Yu and Li Zai, associates in Li Tan's rebellion, were pursued to judgment.
s0390.idiomatic: On dingmao day the cases of wanhu Zhang Bangzhi, his brothers, and twenty-seven others including Jiang Yu and Li Zai, associates in Li Tan's rebellion, were prosecuted.

s0391.literal: On wuchen day, grain rations were issued to newly submitted garrison troops.
s0391.idiomatic: On wuchen day grain rations were issued to newly submitted garrison troops.

s0392.literal: King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent his minister Jin Lu bearing tribute.
s0392.idiomatic: King Wang Chon of Goryeo sent his minister Jin Lu with tribute.

s0393.literal: Fifth month, on yihai day, an edict dispatched Suotuoyan and Guo Shoujing to inspect the river and canal works of Western Xia and submit maps.
s0393.idiomatic: On yihai day of the fifth month an edict sent Suotuoyan and Guo Shoujing to inspect Western Xia's river and canal works and submit maps.

s0394.literal: On gengchen day, an edict ordered the Jian Prefecture garrison commander to divide troops to hold Jianmen and establish a relay at Rentou Mountain.
s0394.idiomatic: On gengchen day an edict ordered the Jian Prefecture garrison commander to detach troops for Jianmen and open a relay station at Rentou Mountain.

s0395.literal: On bingxu day, the moon encroached on Fang.
s0395.idiomatic: On bingxu day the moon passed through Fang.

s0396.literal: On dinghai day, fifty-seven private Song merchants were released, given grain, and sent home to their country.
s0396.idiomatic: On dinghai day fifty-seven private Song merchants were freed, given grain, and sent home.

s0397.literal: On jichou day, because Pingyin County Magistrate Ma Qin had issued six hundred shi of his private grain to feed starving people and also gave the people more than four hundred shi of seed grain, an edict praised and encouraged him and specially granted one bolt of western brocade to honor his righteousness.
s0397.idiomatic: On jichou day Pingyin county magistrate Ma Qin was praised and rewarded with a bolt of western brocade for distributing six hundred shi of his own grain to the starving and more than four hundred shi of seed grain besides.

s0398.literal: On yiwei day, express relay stations in Sichuan were first established.
s0398.idiomatic: On yiwei day express relay stations in Sichuan were established for the first time.

s0399.literal: On bingshen day, ten thousand taels of silver were granted to Prince Qincha to relieve the impoverished among his followers.
s0399.idiomatic: On bingshen day Prince Qincha received ten thousand taels of silver to relieve the poor among his followers.

s0400.literal: On jihai day, the moon encroached on Mao.
s0400.idiomatic: On jihai day the moon passed through Mao.
